# What /assess measures

<!-- Generated by skills/assess/scripts/gen_catalog.py (`make catalog`); do not edit by hand. -->

This page lists every check `/assess` and `/fleet` run, what each one reads, and how it
feeds the maturity model. It is generated from these files, so it changes only when they do:

- `skills/assess/checks/core.toml`
- `skills/assess/checks/core/*.toml`
- `skills/assess/levels/default.toml`
- `skills/assess/scripts/lib/scoring/level_signals.py`
- `skills/assess/scripts/lib/run/signals.py`
- `skills/assess/scripts/lib/run/scan_registry.py`

The same data for machines is [measures.json](../skills/assess/references/measures.json).

Nothing here is a judgement of a team. A gap is the next thing to try, and a check that
could not be read is shown as not measured with its reason: it earns nothing and costs
nothing.

## How evidence is graded

Each signal has an input class: what its producer read. The class fixes a grade. Conditions graded measured or verified count toward a level; conditions graded config_only or declared are listed, not counted.

| Grade | Input classes | Counts toward a level |
|---|---|---|
| `config_only` | `config_text` | no, listed |
| `declared` | `head_text` | no, listed |
| `measured` | `execution_artifact`, `git_history`, `head_structure` | yes |
| `verified` | `ci_executed`, `platform` | yes |

A scan that feeds no maturity-model criterion is `unclassified` until its evidence is classified (#789 step 6).

## Conditions by truth tag

Each condition carries one or more truth tags: the truth it keeps honest. A condition holds when all of its criteria hold, and each criterion's key is `<row>.<n>:<signal>`. A condition with several tags is listed under its first tag and named under the others as shared; a level result counts it once. Conditions are sorted by id.

- Behaviour (`behaviour`)
- Contracts (`contracts`)
- Docs (`docs`)
- Structure (`structure`)
- Agent context (`agent_context`)
- Agent runtime (`agent_runtime`)
- Governance (`governance`)
- Supply chain (`supply_chain`)

### Behaviour

That the code's behaviour is checked by something that runs on every change, not taken on trust.

| Condition | Producer | Criterion | Grade | Counts | Step gate | Polarity | Links | Exit review | Why it matters | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-skip-label.1` A label skips every CI check on pull requests | `ci_hazards` | Pull request labels that skip every CI check: is above 0 (`ci_hazards.skip_labels gt 0`) | `measured` | no, listed | held while met: `ci_runs_tests` | hazard | - | - | A label that skips every check lets any pull request merge on a green that no test produced. An agent, or a person in a hurry, needs only to add the label. | Drop the label condition from the jobs' if: lines, or limit it to jobs that check nothing, such as docs previews. If a skip is needed, scope it with a paths filter so the checks still run on code changes. |
| `ci-test-failures-ignored.1` CI ignores test failures | `ci_hazards` | Committed files that set Maven to ignore test failures: is above 0 (`ci_hazards.test_failures_ignored gt 0`) | `measured` | no, listed | held while met: `ci_runs_tests` | hazard | - | - | With broken tests ignored, the build passes whatever the tests report, so a green run says nothing about the change. A test an agent broke reaches the main branch unseen. | Remove -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true and testFailureIgnore from the CI command, the Jenkinsfile and the poms listed. Quarantine a flaky test by name instead of ignoring every failure. |
| `layer-5-ci.1` CI runs your tests or linters, and an error stops the job | `ci_checks` | A CI check runs on ordinary changes and can stop its job: is true (`ci_checks.enforced_check_runs eq true`) | `verified` | yes | `ci_runs_tests` | positive | - | - | This turns "the agent says it works" into "CI says it works": a check that can stop its job runs on ordinary changes, so a broken change turns the job red where everyone can see it. | Add a CI step that runs your test or lint command on pull requests, without \|\| true, continue-on-error or allow_failure. |
| `layer-6-coverage.1` CI runs a coverage gate of at least 50 percent | `coverage_gate` | CI runs a coverage gate of at least 50 percent: is true (`coverage_gate.enforced_meets_minimum eq true`) | `verified` | yes | `coverage_gate` | positive | - | - | An enforced floor turns the job red when a change takes coverage below it, so tests an agent removes or skips show in CI instead of passing quietly. | Set a fail_under (or your tool's threshold) of at least 50 percent, written as a number, near your current coverage. Run the coverage check in a CI step on pull requests (pytest --cov, not plain pytest), without \|\| true or continue-on-error. Then CI keeps coverage at the level you have reached. |
| `layer-6-coverage.2` A mutation run has completed | `test_pressure` | A mutation run completed: is true (`test_pressure.mutation_run eq true`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | requires `layer-5-ci.1` | - | Coverage shows tests run the code; a mutation run shows whether they notice it changing. A completed run names the surviving mutants, which are the tests an agent cannot yet rely on. | Run the opt-in mutation pass to see which tests pin behaviour. |
| `skill-script-tests.1` Each skill's scripts have tests beside them (presence, not coverage) | `skill_script_tests` | Skills whose scripts have no tests beside them: is 0 (`skill_script_tests.skills_untested eq 0`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | - | - | A skill's scripts run with an agent's permissions every time it triggers; tests beside them are the only check that a change still does what the SKILL.md promises. | Add tests for each named skill's scripts in that skill's own folder (tests/ or test_*.py beside them); where the report finds them elsewhere, move or copy them in, since tests outside the folder do not ship with the skill. |

### Contracts

That generated output and its source agree, so an agent editing one does not quietly break the other.

| Condition | Producer | Criterion | Grade | Counts | Step gate | Polarity | Links | Exit review | Why it matters | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `api-compat.1` API compatibility checked by CI (shared with Structure) | `api_compat` | CI runs an API compatibility check: is true (`api_compat.present eq true`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | - | - | An agent changing code cannot see who depends on its public names. A compatibility tool CI runs against the last release, or a test that pins the exports, turns the job red on a change that breaks a caller, so the contract holds without a reviewer catching it. | Run a compatibility check in CI: cargo semver-checks, buf breaking or api-extractor run. apidiff only prints a report, so exit 1 when its output lists a change. japicmp needs --error-on-* or a breakBuild* setting. Or run a test that compares the exports with a fixed list. |

| `doc-freshness.2` Four in five mapped docs keep pace | `doc_staleness` | Share of mapped docs outrun by their code: is at most 20 (`doc_staleness.summary.stale_pct lte 20`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | - | - | With four in five mapped docs keeping pace with their code, an agent can take most of what it reads at its word. | Refresh the docs the report lists under doc freshness, oldest first. |

### Structure

That the code is shaped so an agent can work on one part without holding the whole repository in mind.

| Condition | Producer | Criterion | Grade | Counts | Step gate | Polarity | Links | Exit review | Why it matters | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layer-2-design.1` The import graph has module structure | `structure` | Import-graph modularity: is at least 0.3 (`structure.modularity_q gte 0.3`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | - | - | Clear modules let an agent load the part of the code a task touches, instead of tracing the whole repository to change one thing. | Group related modules into packages that mostly import within themselves. |
| `layer-2-design.2` Packages import one another | `structure` | Cross-package imports: is above 0 (`structure.cross_package_edges gt 0`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | requires `layer-2-design.1` | - | A guard for the next condition: with no import between packages, the front-door share reads null by default and says nothing about how packages are entered. | Nothing to change on its own: this is met once one package imports another. |
| `layer-2-design.2` Cross-package imports use a package's front door | `structure` | Cross-package imports through a package's front door: is at least 0.9 (`structure.front_door_ratio gte 0.9`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | requires `layer-2-design.1` | - | When packages are entered through one public surface, an agent can change a package's insides without breaking callers it never read. | Import other packages through their public API rather than their submodules. |
| `layer-3-linters.1` CI runs a linter or type checker | `ci_checks` | A CI line runs a linter on ordinary changes and can stop its job: is true (`ci_checks.lint_runs eq true`) | `verified` | yes | - | positive | - | - | A linter or type checker in CI catches mechanical mistakes in every change, an agent's included, before a reviewer spends time on them. | Add a CI step that runs your linter (ruff check ., eslint, mypy, make lint) on pull requests, without \|\| true, continue-on-error or allow_failure. |
| `layer-3-linters.2` Stale suppressions stay at 10 or fewer | `promissory_markers` | Stale suppression comments: is at most 10 (`promissory_markers.families.suppression.stale lte 10`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | requires `layer-3-linters.1` | - | A suppression that survives many edits switches a check off in code that keeps changing, and an agent editing nearby gets no sign the warning still matters. | Revisit the oldest suppression comments and fix or remove them. |
| `layer-3-linters.2` Suppression ages can be read from history | `promissory_markers` | Marker aging is reliable: is true (`promissory_markers.aging_reliable eq true`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | requires `layer-3-linters.1` | - | A guard for the suppression count: on a shallow or squashed history every suppression looks new, so a count of 0 would say nothing. | Run on a full clone so suppression ages can be measured. |

Tests and fixtures are counted apart, so many small ones cannot hide a large source file. Generated-header files are left out; Elixir @moduledoc and @doc lines do not count. | Split the largest files along their natural seams. |

That an agent starts each task knowing how this repository works and how to check its own change.

### Agent runtime

That an agent can see the system it changes run, and confirm a change there, not only in the code.

| Condition | Producer | Criterion | Grade | Counts | Step gate | Polarity | Links | Exit review | Why it matters | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-evals.1` Agent eval suites run in CI with a baseline (shared with Behaviour) | `ci_model_jobs` | An agent eval suite runs in CI against a committed baseline: is true (`ci_model_jobs.agent_evals.present eq true`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | - | - | A prompt or model change can make an agent worse while every unit test still passes. Eval cases run in CI against a committed baseline turn that drop into a red check, and the baseline in the tree says what passing means. | Keep the agent's eval cases in an evals/ folder and commit a baseline beside them: a snapshot, recorded model responses or a tool-budget file. Run the folder from a CI job, gated to prompt and model changes if it costs money. |
| `agent-job-write-access.1` An agent job holds write access (shared with Governance) | `agent_ops` | Agent jobs with a write scope and no separate writer job: is above 0 (`agent_ops.summary.agent_job_write_access gt 0`) | `measured` | no, listed | - | hazard | - | - | An agent job with a write scope and no separate writer job can push, merge or edit issues on the strength of text an outsider wrote, with nothing between the prompt and the write. | Drop the write scopes from the agent job's `permissions:` and do the writes in a job that `needs:` it, or in gh-aw `safe-outputs:`. A turn or budget cap limits cost, not what the token can do. |
| `agent-least-privilege.1` Agent jobs run with least privilege (shared with Governance) | `agent_ops` | Every agent job runs with a read-only token: is true (`agent_ops.summary.agent_jobs_least_privilege eq true`) | `measured` | yes | - | positive | - | - | An agent acts on whatever text reaches its prompt, an issue body or a pull request included. A read-only token keeps a misled agent from pushing, merging or editing issues itself; a separate job that acts on its output does the writing, where a reviewer can see each write. | Give each job that runs an agent `permissions:` with no write scope, such as `contents: read` or `read-all`. Move writes into a separate job that `needs:` the agent job, or into gh-aw `safe-outputs:`. A job-level `permissions:` replaces the workflow's, so check the agent job's own block. |
| `layer-1-liveness.1` Some runtime telemetry is committed | `observability` | Observability rung: is at least 1 (`observability.rung gte 1`) | `declared` | no, listed | - | positive | - | - | Telemetry in the code is what any view of the running system is built on. Without it, there is nothing for an agent or a person to read when checking how a change behaves in use. | Add a telemetry dependency, a runbook or an OBSERVABILITY.md so an agent can see the system run. |

Or add a template checkbox that asks the author to disclose AI assistance. Then enforce it with a workflow that reads the disclosure. |

- `contracts` and `structure`: `api-compat.1`

- `agent_runtime` and `governance`: `agent-least-privilege.1`

### Step gates

The autonomy Steps in order. A Step needs every gate, whatever the gate's grade, and nothing else: no count of conditions moves a Step. Gates accumulate, so each Step keeps the gates below it.

| Step | Name | New gates | Gate covers | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Assisted | - | - | - |
| 2 | Supervised agent PRs | `instructions` | `layer-0-instructions.1` | `agent_context` |
| 3 | Unattended agent PRs | `ci_runs_tests` | `layer-5-ci.1` | `behaviour` |
| 4 | Autonomous loops | `coverage_gate` | `layer-6-coverage.1` | `behaviour` |

## Scans

Every scan name `assess_signals.py --scans` accepts, sorted by name.

### `accretion_ratchet`: Accretion ratchet

Files that only ever grow get harder to read whole with every addition; this names them before an agent adds the next feature to one.

- Collector: `core.accretion_ratchet`, reading `accretion_scan`, `current`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: only a full /assess run builds it; headless and fleet runs report it not measured.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `accretion_ratchet.reason` drop.
- Used by: finding `accretion_ratchet`.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when:
  - `not_registered`: Only a full /assess run builds this block; a headless or fleet run reports it not measured. Run /assess on the repository to measure it.

### `agent_building`: Agent building

Run plumbing: no row or finding reads this scan.

- Collector: `core.agent_building`, reading `repo_root`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `agent_building.agent_class` token, `agent_building.ci_agents` token, `agent_building.config` token, `agent_building.git_hosts` token, `agent_building.issue_trackers` token, `agent_building.reason` drop, `agent_building.sdks` token.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

### `agent_consistency`: Cross-agent instruction consistency

It compares the instruction files of every agent system present, so each agent is told the same checks and thresholds, from one source.

Compares the root instruction files of every agent system present: Claude Code, AGENTS.md, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Aider, Junie, Amazon Q, Kiro, Continue and Zed. It finds check commands one file names and another does not, and thresholds that conflict. It checks whether each file links to one canonical file, and gives the pointer line for each system that does not.

- Collector: `core.agent_consistency`, reading `repo_root`, `excludes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `agent_consistency.canonical` path, `agent_consistency.conflicts_reason` token, `agent_consistency.divergences.kind` token, `agent_consistency.divergences.missing_from` token, `agent_consistency.divergences.named_in` token, `agent_consistency.divergences.stated.system` token, `agent_consistency.divergences.value` drop, `agent_consistency.files.link` token, `agent_consistency.files.path` path, `agent_consistency.files.system` token, `agent_consistency.next_steps.path` path, `agent_consistency.next_steps.pointer` drop, `agent_consistency.next_steps.symlink` drop, `agent_consistency.next_steps.system` token, `agent_consistency.not_read` drop, `agent_consistency.systems` token, `agent_consistency.unlinked_reason` token.
- Used by: row `agent-consistency`.
- Evidence: `agent_consistency.conflicts` head_structure (measured), `agent_consistency.unlinked` head_structure (measured).
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `agent_consistency.conflicts` feeds `agent-consistency.1:agent_consistency.conflicts`: When agent systems are told different check commands or thresholds, one agent's change passes checks another agent was told to run differently.
- `agent_consistency.unlinked` feeds `agent-consistency.2:agent_consistency.unlinked`: One source of instructions keeps every agent's picture of the repository the same, and keeps it maintained in one place.

### `agent_environment`: Agent working environment

It reads what an agent needs to work like CI does: the check command its instructions name, the committed setup and a lockfile for each dependency manifest.

Committed agent setup, the check command an instruction file names, lockfiles per manifest, and the CI cap. The CI-duration probe is off in headless runs. A manifest row's note is skipped_library or direct_pins_only. skipped_library is a library whose ecosystem commits no lock: it is listed, and not counted in manifests_total or unlocked_total. direct_pins_only is a Gradle version catalog or NuGet central package management with no lock: it counts as unlocked.

- Collector: `core.agent_environment`, reading `repo_root`, `instruction_files`, `agent_harness`, `excludes`.
- Network: yes, GitHub or GitLab.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `agent_environment.check.entry_points.command` drop, `agent_environment.check.entry_points.source` drop, `agent_environment.check.named.command` drop, `agent_environment.check.named.reason` drop, `agent_environment.check.named.verdict` token, `agent_environment.check.unresolved.command` drop, `agent_environment.check.unresolved.reason` drop, `agent_environment.check.unresolved.verdict` token, `agent_environment.ci_duration.branch` drop, `agent_environment.ci_duration.reason` drop, `agent_environment.ci_duration.workflows.workflow` drop, `agent_environment.findings.detail` drop, `agent_environment.findings.fix` drop, `agent_environment.findings.kind` token, `agent_environment.layer5_cap.ceiling` token, `agent_environment.layer5_cap.reason` drop, `agent_environment.layer5_cap.unmet` token, `agent_environment.pinning.manifests.ecosystem` token, `agent_environment.pinning.manifests.lockfile` path, `agent_environment.pinning.manifests.manifest` path, `agent_environment.pinning.manifests.note` token, `agent_environment.reason` drop, `agent_environment.setup.sources.detail` drop, `agent_environment.setup.sources.kind` token.
- Used by: row `layer-0-instructions`, row `layer-5-ci`.
- Evidence: `agent_environment.check.named_total` head_text (declared), `agent_environment.pinning.unlocked_total` head_text (declared).
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `agent_environment.check.named_total` feeds `layer-0-instructions.2:agent_environment.check.named_total`: An agent can confirm its change only if it knows which command checks it. A named command that resolves saves it guessing, and running the wrong check or none.
- `agent_environment.pinning.unlocked_total` feeds `layer-5-ci.2:agent_environment.pinning.unlocked_total`: A committed lockfile means an agent installs the dependency versions CI tested, so a local test result matches CI's.

### `agent_harness`: Committed agent harness

Committed hooks, env blocks and MCP servers run in every agent session, headless ones included; this lists what they run and flags any that expose a secret or widen an agent's reach.

- Collector: `core.agent_harness`, reading `repo_root`, `scope`, `excludes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `agent_harness.executes.detail` drop, `agent_harness.executes.kind` token, `agent_harness.executes.name` drop, `agent_harness.findings.detail` drop, `agent_harness.findings.fix` drop, `agent_harness.findings.kind` token, `agent_harness.reason` drop.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

### `agent_ops`: Agent-operations guardrails

Committed allowlists, hooks, sandbox rules and routines make an agent's limits and repeated work the same on every clone, and reviewable like code.

Committed permission allowlists, hooks, sandbox rules and routines. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and VS Code settings and hook files count as one set. A routine is a routine file, or a workflow that runs an agent on a schedule or an issue or pull request event. For each workflow job that runs an agent, its effective token scope and whether its writes go through a separate job. Whether an agent job that can write files can rewrite an instruction file or its own workflow with no CODEOWNERS owner on it.

- Collector: `core.agent_ops`, reading `repo_root`, `managed_settings`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `agent_ops.agent_instruction_rewrite_files` path, `agent_ops.agent_instruction_rewrite_unread_files` path, `agent_ops.agent_jobs.job` drop, `agent_ops.agent_jobs.path` path, `agent_ops.agent_jobs.scope` token, `agent_ops.agent_jobs.write_scopes` token, `agent_ops.agent_workflows.path` path, `agent_ops.agent_workflows.signs` token, `agent_ops.agent_workflows.triggers` token, `agent_ops.agent_workflows.via` path, `agent_ops.managed.reason` token, `agent_ops.managed.sources.kind` token, `agent_ops.managed.state` token, `agent_ops.settings.default_mode` token, `agent_ops.settings.tool` token, `agent_ops.summary.agent_instruction_rewrite_reason` token, `agent_ops.summary.agent_job_write_access_reason` token, `agent_ops.summary.agent_jobs_least_privilege_reason` token, `agent_ops.summary.agent_work_present_reason` token, `agent_ops.summary.permissions_encoded_reason` token, `agent_ops.summary.permissions_source` token.
- Used by: row `agent-job-write-access`, row `agent-least-privilege`, row `agent-rewrites-instructions`, row `layer-8-agent-ops`.
- Evidence: `agent_ops.summary.agent_instruction_rewrite` head_structure (measured), `agent_ops.summary.agent_job_write_access` head_structure (measured), `agent_ops.summary.agent_jobs_least_privilege` head_structure (measured), `agent_ops.summary.agent_work_present` head_text (declared), `agent_ops.summary.hooks_present` config_text (config_only), `agent_ops.summary.permissions_encoded` config_text (config_only).
- Not measured when:
  - `agent_workflows_unread`: A workflow calls an unread reusable workflow in another repository whose path names an agent. Agent work: a scheduled or event-triggered caller, and no local agent workflow. Job scope: a caller on any trigger without a read-only scope, and no local agent job that settles it. Nothing to change: this reads as not measured until that workflow can be read.
  - `no_agent_jobs`: With agent_job_count at 0, no committed workflow job runs an agent, so there is no agent job scope to read. Nothing to change.
  - `agent_job_scope_unread`: An agent job's permissions could not be read. They may be an expression or an unknown value, or the agent sign sits outside every job. No other agent job settles the reading. Write the agent job's permissions as a plain map, such as contents: read, so the scan can read it.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `agent_ops.summary.agent_job_write_access` feeds `agent-job-write-access.1:agent_ops.summary.agent_job_write_access`: An agent job with a write scope and no separate writer job can push, merge or edit issues on the strength of text an outsider wrote, with nothing between the prompt and the write.
- `agent_ops.summary.agent_jobs_least_privilege` feeds `agent-least-privilege.1:agent_ops.summary.agent_jobs_least_privilege`: An agent acts on whatever text reaches its prompt, an issue body or a pull request included. A read-only token keeps a misled agent from pushing, merging or editing issues itself; a separate job that acts on its output does the writing, where a reviewer can see each write.
- `agent_ops.summary.agent_instruction_rewrite` feeds `agent-rewrites-instructions.1:agent_ops.summary.agent_instruction_rewrite`: An agent job that can push files can change AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or its own workflow, so the next run follows instructions no reviewer approved. CI then checks changes against rules the agent wrote for itself.
- `agent_ops.summary.permissions_encoded` feeds `layer-8-agent-ops.1:agent_ops.summary.permissions_encoded`: Deny rules and hooks keep an agent inside its limits in every permission mode, auto mode included. Committed to the repository or set in managed settings, they apply the same way to everyone and are reviewed like code.
- `agent_ops.summary.hooks_present` feeds `layer-8-agent-ops.2:agent_ops.summary.hooks_present`: Committed hooks run around an agent's actions on every clone, so a check written once applies without the agent having to remember it.
- `agent_ops.summary.agent_work_present` feeds `layer-8-agent-ops.2:agent_ops.summary.agent_work_present`: Committed routines define the agent work the repository runs on a schedule or trigger, so it runs the same way each time and is reviewed like code.

### `agent_outcome`: Agent commit outcomes

No other scan says whether agent work holds once it lands; this records the share of agent commits later reverted or rewritten within two weeks, as a history to set beside the gates. Nothing scores it.

- Collector: `core.agent_outcome`, reading `repo_root`, `scope`, `history_window`, `fleet_config`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.

### `ai_governance`: AI governance

A policy on AI contributions holds only when something checks it. A workflow that reads each pull request for disclosure turns the policy into a rule an agent meets on every change; a policy file or a checkbox alone asks for it and checks nothing.

Whether a workflow on pull requests reads the body or commit trailers for AI disclosure, then turns the check red or adds a label. It also lists an AI_POLICY.md at a fixed path and template checkboxes that ask for AI disclosure. It lists Copilot instruction files that decline Copilot review for the whole repository.

- Not measured when:

  - `ruby_unread`: No step reads as enforcing AI disclosure, but a step on a pull request workflow runs Ruby that names an AI marker. This reader does not read Ruby, so that step may enforce it. Nothing to change: this reads as not measured while the check is in Ruby. A shell, Python or JavaScript check is read.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `ai_governance.policy_declared` feeds `ai-policy-declared.1:ai_governance.policy_declared`: A written policy tells contributors and agents what the project expects of AI-assisted work. It is listed, not counted: a file or a checkbox asks for the practice, and only a check that reads it shows the practice holds.
- `ai_governance.enforced` feeds `ai-policy-enforced.1:ai_governance.enforced`: An agent follows the rules a check holds it to. A workflow that reads each pull request for AI disclosure or attribution, and turns the check red or labels on it, applies the policy to every change, an agent's included, without a reviewer having to remember it.

### `api_compat`: API compatibility checks CI runs

A public interface stays stable only when a check stops a breaking change. A compatibility tool CI runs, or a test that pins the exports, turns an agent's accidental break of a contract into a red check, not a downstream bug report.

Whether a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI step runs an API compatibility tool: apidiff, api-extractor, griffe check, cargo semver-checks, buf breaking, japicmp or revapi. The step may run it through a committed script, a make recipe, a Maven or Gradle build, or a package.json script. Whether a test pins the public exports while CI runs tests. A tool named only in a build file is listed as declared, never counted.

  - `ci_not_read`: A compatibility tool is named in a build file, or found in a form whose exit status the step may hide. A CI file this reader cannot follow may run it. Examples are a CI system it does not parse, a GitLab include, or a step the follower could not settle. Nothing to change if the tool runs; calling it from a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI step the scan reads lets it count.

Why the signals named here matter:

A compatibility tool CI runs against the last release, or a test that pins the exports, turns the job red on a change that breaks a caller, so the contract holds without a reviewer catching it.

### `backlog_ready`: Backlog kept agent-ready (intake configuration)

An agent handed an issue with no structure, never triaged and judged against no written bar starts from a guess; intake that asks for structure and a documented ready label is the bar an issue clears before an agent picks it up.

How new issues are taken in and answered. An issue form has a required field, or a GitLab issue template has the six definition-of-ready sections. A workflow on issues opened adds an untriaged label, or on GitLab the refinement template is included or a scheduled job adds one. A ready label is documented with its criteria. No stale job can close a ready issue. The tracker itself is read too: time to a first response, the untriaged share and issues closed over opened.

- Collector: `core.backlog_ready`, reading `repo_root`, `backlog_outcomes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `backlog_ready.close_open_met_reason` token, `backlog_ready.close_open_ratio_reason` token, `backlog_ready.first_response_median_days_reason` token, `backlog_ready.first_response_met_reason` token, `backlog_ready.outcomes.reason` token, `backlog_ready.required_form_field_reason` token, `backlog_ready.stale_job_safe_reason` token, `backlog_ready.untriaged_after_7d_share_reason` token, `backlog_ready.untriaged_met_reason` token, `backlog_ready.untriaged_on_open_reason` token.
- Used by: row `backlog-ready`.
- Evidence: `backlog_ready.close_open_met` platform (verified), `backlog_ready.first_response_met` platform (verified), `backlog_ready.ready_label_documented` config_text (config_only), `backlog_ready.required_form_field` config_text (config_only), `backlog_ready.stale_job_safe` config_text (config_only), `backlog_ready.untriaged_met` platform (verified), `backlog_ready.untriaged_on_open` config_text (config_only).
- Not measured when:
  - `form_unreadable`: No issue form read has a required field, and a GitHub issue form could not be read. Causes are a tab indent, an unclosed flow collection, no top-level body list, or a file over the size limit. Fix the form so GitHub accepts it; a form GitHub rejects is not offered to the person opening an issue.
  - `gitlab_template_unreadable`: No form or template read meets the bar. A GitLab issue template could not be read: it is too large or could not be opened. Nothing to change if the template has the six sections; a GitLab issue template under the size limit lets the scan read its headings.
  - `gitlab_ci_unreadable`: No workflow adds an untriaged label, and .gitlab-ci.yml has a tab in its indentation or an unclosed flow collection, which GitLab rejects. Fix .gitlab-ci.yml so GitLab accepts it; the pipeline editor's validate tab names the line.
  - `gitlab_ci_unsettled`: No workflow or GitLab job read adds an untriaged label on a schedule. But something this reader cannot follow may: an include not read offline, or an anchor merge, !reference, variable label or unread rule. Nothing to change if a scheduled job labels new issues; a literal label, plain rules: and a local include let the scan read it.
  - `workflow_unreadable`: No workflow read adds an untriaged label when an issue opens, and a workflow's on: key could not be read. Nothing to change if that workflow labels new issues; a plain on: issues: types: [opened] lets the scan read it.
  - `stale_input_unresolved`: No stale job is sure to close a ready issue. But one sets its close days or exempt labels to an expression, which this reader does not follow. Nothing to change if the job exempts the ready label; a literal exempt-issue-labels or days-before-issue-close: -1 lets the scan read it.
  - `no_network`: The issue tracker was not read: a headless run without --platform, or the host could not be reached. Run /assess with gh or glab signed in, or a headless run with --platform.
  - `no_platform_auth`: The issue tracker could not be read: gh or glab is missing or signed out, or the token was refused the issues. Sign gh or glab in with a token that can read the repository's issues, then run again.
  - `unsupported_host`: The repository has no remote, or its host is not GitHub or a GitLab that glab reaches, so its issues were not read. Nothing to change if the tracker lives elsewhere; for a self-managed GitLab, sign glab in to the host.
  - `platform_error`: A read of the issue tracker failed for a reason other than access, such as a rate limit or a server error. Run again later.
  - `empty_window`: The metric has nothing to measure yet: no issue in the window, none answered, or no open issue older than 7 days. Nothing to change; the metric reads once there are issues to measure.
  - `response_unread`: A first response may exist that was not read: a long timeline, the note cap or an unclassified account. Run again with gh or glab signed in as an account that can read users; the caps are fixed.
  - `window_truncated`: The window's issue list passed the read cap, so issues may be missing. The ratio is not taken, nor the median when no issue read was answered. Nothing to change; set a shorter window_days in [backlog_ready] to read the whole window.
  - `open_truncated`: The open-issue list passed the read cap, so the untriaged share would cover only part of it and is not taken. Nothing to change; close or triage old open issues to bring the list under the cap.
  - `response_pending`: The median wait is not settled yet: issues still unanswered could put it either side of first_response_max_days, depending on when they are answered. Answer, label or close the open new issues; the condition settles once their waits decide the median.
  - `no_response`: No issue opened in the window got a first response from a person, and each has waited longer than first_response_max_days. Answer, label or close new issues within first_response_max_days.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `backlog_ready.first_response_met` feeds `backlog-ready.2:backlog_ready.first_response_met`: A ready label and an issue form nobody acts on are intent, not practice: issues answered, triaged and closed at the pace they open are what keep the backlog an agent draws from current.

### `ci_checks`: CI runs a test or lint command

It reads whether CI runs tests or linters on ordinary changes in a way that can stop the job, so "it passed" means a check ran and could have said no.

Whether a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI line runs a test or lint command. Whether such a line can fail its job on ordinary changes: not masked, and not outside the ordinary triggers. Whether such a line runs a linter. The value is null when no check is found but a CI file pulls its jobs from elsewhere. It is also null when no check is found and the tree tracks a CI file the scan does not parse. It is null under --platform when most sampled merged pull requests carry an external CI check. It is null when a root Prow OWNERS_ALIASES is the only CI evidence.

- Collector: `core.ci_checks`, reading `repo_root`, `ghsync_root`, `gitlab_merged_ci`, `external_ci`, `gitlab_include_renames`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `ci_checks.basis` token, `ci_checks.enforced_basis` token, `ci_checks.includes.id` id, `ci_checks.includes.kind` token, `ci_checks.includes.ref_basis` token, `ci_checks.includes.rename` token, `ci_checks.includes.status` token, `ci_checks.lint_basis` token, `ci_checks.merged_config` token, `ci_checks.merged_config_reason` token, `ci_checks.reason` drop.
- Used by: row `layer-3-linters`, row `layer-5-ci`.
- Evidence: `ci_checks.enforced_check_runs` ci_executed (verified), `ci_checks.lint_runs` ci_executed (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `included_jobs`: A CI file pulls its jobs from a file this checkout does not hold, so the check may live there. Nothing to change: this reads as not measured until the included file can be read. On GitLab, fleet --platform reads the merged configuration through the CI lint API.
  - `merged_config_partial`: GitLab's merged CI configuration was read and runs no check, but jobs may be missing from it. The lint API does not expand an include under rules: or a trigger: child pipeline. Nothing to change: a check in a conditional include or child pipeline is not read, so this stays not measured rather than reading false.
  - `unknown_trigger`: In enforced_basis: an unmasked check sits in a workflow or job whose triggers this reader cannot settle. Examples are a missing on: key, or a rules: if: on a custom variable. Nothing to change if it runs on every change; naming push or pull_request, or a merge request rule, lets the scan read it.
  - `check_may_pass`: In enforced_basis and lint_basis: the check's exit status may not reach its job. Causes are a || fallback that can pass (pytest || echo failed), an if or while condition, or an until loop that breaks. Or a check sits before && with more of the step after it, or in a { } group or function. Let the check's exit status reach the step. Run the check on its own line, or end the fallback with exit 1 (pytest || { echo failed; exit 1; }).
  - `script_not_found`: In enforced_basis and lint_basis: the only CI line that would settle the signal runs a committed script (./ci.sh, bash scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/lint.sh). No tracked file matches that script, so it is not credited. An earlier step may still create it. Commit the script the CI step runs. Or call the test or lint command in its own CI step (pytest, ruff check .), so the scan can read it.
  - `check_target`: No CI line runs the linter (lint_basis) or the check (enforced_basis). But one runs a target whose recipe is not read, and that target may run it. Examples: make check or npm test for a linter; make foo, npm run foo or ./scripts/foo.sh for a check. Nothing to change if the target runs the check; calling the test or lint command in its own CI step (make test, pytest, ruff check .) lets the scan read it.
  - `unread_ci_system`: No readable GitHub Actions or GitLab CI line settles the signal. The tree tracks a CI file of a system this scan does not parse, such as Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite, LUCI, Prow or Zuul. The lib/unread_ci.py docstring lists the paths, and unread_ci_files counts them. Nothing to change: the scanner cannot read those systems' configuration, so their checks read as not measured rather than absent.
  - `external_ci`: Under --platform only: no readable CI line settles the signal. Over half of sampled merged pull requests carry a check run or status from a known external CI system (Buildkite, LUCI, Prow tide, Azure Pipelines). A check ran; that earns no credit. Nothing to change: the checks run on a CI system configured outside the repository, so they read as not measured rather than absent.
  - `external_ci_marker`: The tree tracks no CI file of any kind, and the root holds a Prow OWNERS_ALIASES file. So presubmits likely run on Prow, configured in another repository. An OWNERS file alone is not a marker. Nothing to change: run with --platform to read the checks on merged pull requests instead.
  - `analysers_in_build`: In lint_basis: no CI line runs a linter, but a CI dotnet build runs the analysers a committed Directory.Build.props or .csproj turns on (EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, AnalysisLevel). Their severities live in .editorconfig, which the scan does not evaluate. Nothing to change if the analysers fail the build on a finding; a CI step running dotnet format --verify-no-changes lets the scan read a lint run.
  - `compiler_gate_only`: In lint_basis: no CI line runs a linter, and the only static gate is a compiler run with warnings as errors. Examples are mix compile --warnings-as-errors, -Werror, dotnet build -warnaserror and TreatWarningsAsErrors in Directory.Build.props. It is not counted as a lint run. Running a linter or analyser in its own CI step (mix credo, clang-tidy, dotnet format --verify-no-changes) lets the scan read a lint run.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `ci_checks.lint_runs` feeds `layer-3-linters.1:ci_checks.lint_runs`: A linter or type checker in CI catches mechanical mistakes in every change, an agent's included, before a reviewer spends time on them.
- `ci_checks.enforced_check_runs` feeds `layer-5-ci.1:ci_checks.enforced_check_runs`: This turns "the agent says it works" into "CI says it works": a check that can stop its job runs on ordinary changes, so a broken change turns the job red where everyone can see it.

### `ci_hazards`: CI that can be told not to fail

Pull request labels that skip every check job of every GitHub Actions workflow that runs a check on pull requests. Committed files that tell Maven to ignore test failures. It reads CI files, Jenkinsfiles, .mvn/maven.config and reactor poms. It also reads the scripts, make recipes, local actions and poms a CI step leads to. Why the signals named here matter:

- `ci_hazards.instructions_unchecked` feeds `ci-instructions-unchecked.1:ci_hazards.instructions_unchecked`: When every pull request check filters the instruction file out, a change to it merges with no check run. Agents follow that file, so an edit that breaks it reaches every agent unseen.

### `ci_model_jobs`: Model-backed CI jobs

A CI job that calls a model costs money on every run. If it runs on every merge and every pull request update, the cost grows with the number of changes agents make, not with changes to the prompts it tests.

For each job, whether a gate stops it running on every push or pull request update. Gates are a paths filter, a schedule or manual trigger only, a label, or GitLab rules:changes. Examples are an unreadable on: key, a label if: joined with ||, or a job that only names a provider secret. A GitLab merge that is not settled reads the same way. Nothing to change if the job is gated; a plain paths:, schedule: or label condition lets the scan read it.

### `concurrency`: Concurrency readiness

No other scan says whether many agents can change the repository at once; this records how often the same files, generated ones included, change across merges, the files every parallel change would conflict on. Listed, not counted: nothing scores it.

- Collector: `core.concurrency`, reading `repo_root`, `scope`, `history_window`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `concurrency.fan_in_null_reason` token, `concurrency.hot_files` drop, `concurrency.limits` drop, `concurrency.reason` reason, `concurrency.since` drop, `concurrency.window` token.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when:
  - `short_history`: The window holds fewer than 10 first-parent commits, too few for a share to mean anything. Nothing to change in the repository; a longer --window, or more history, lets the scan read it.
  - `shallow_clone`: The checkout is a shallow clone, so the merges read are cut short. Nothing to change in the repository; a full clone (git fetch --unshallow) lets the scan read it.
  - `shallow_unknown`: Git could not confirm the checkout is a full clone. Nothing to change in the repository; run the scan on a full clone.
  - `not_a_repo`: The path is not a git repository, or one with no commits. Nothing to change: there is no history to read.
  - `no_git`: git is not installed where the scan ran. Install git where the scan runs.
  - `git_failed`: A git read after the first (the merge log or the attribute read) failed on a repository the first read could open. Nothing to change in the repository; re-run the scan, and report the failure if it repeats.
  - `git_timeout`: A git read took longer than the scan allows. Nothing to change in the repository; a shorter --window reads less history.

### `contributor_files`: Contributor files

A contributing guide tells a newcomer, human or agent, how to build, test and shape a change the way the project merges it, and a security policy gives them a private route for a vulnerability instead of a public issue.

A contributing guide and a security policy at the root, in .github/ or in docs/. The policy is a SECURITY file or a link to GitHub private vulnerability reporting. Issue and pull or merge request templates count as evidence.

- Not measured when:
  - `knowledge_base`: The repository is a knowledge base (archetype knowledge-base), which takes no code patches. Nothing to change: a contributing guide and a security policy are not measured for a knowledge base.
  - `org_policy_not_read`: The repository holds no security policy. The owner's shared .github repository, whose policy GitHub shows on this one, was not read. The cause is offline use, no --platform, a remote not on github.com, or gh not signed in. Commit a SECURITY.md, or run /assess with gh signed in (or fleet with --platform) so the owner's shared policy is read.

### `coverage_gate`: Coverage gate

It finds the coverage threshold the repository sets and whether CI enforces it, which is the line that keeps tests from thinning out under a run of changes.

Finds coverage thresholds written in CI, task-runner and tool config, each with its file, line and threshold.

- Collector: `core.coverage_gate`, reading `repo_root`, `scope`, `excludes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `coverage_gate.enforced_basis` token, `coverage_gate.gates.form` drop, `coverage_gate.gates.metric` token, `coverage_gate.gates.tool` token, `coverage_gate.gates.unit` token, `coverage_gate.not_detected` drop, `coverage_gate.unmeasured_reason` token.
- Used by: row `layer-6-coverage`.
- Evidence: `coverage_gate.enforced_meets_minimum` ci_executed (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `go_rust_gate_form_not_read`: A go.mod or Cargo.toml has no coverage gate found for it. No gate of at least 50 percent exists for another language either (a low Python gate beside go.mod is not unmet). Its gate may be a script that compares go tool cover (or a report) to a number, which this scan does not read. Nothing to change if a script gates coverage. To have it measured, set the threshold in go-test-coverage's .testcoverage.yml, cargo tarpaulin --fail-under or cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines.
  - `codecov_target_not_read`: The only coverage gate that could reach 50 percent is a Codecov project status. Its target is auto, missing (Codecov's default is auto) or not a number. So the floor it holds is the base commit's coverage, not a number this scan can compare. Run a coverage threshold of at least 50 percent in a CI step, such as pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80 or a fail_under your CI runs. A numeric Codecov target (target: 80%) makes the threshold readable. Whether branch protection requires the status is not read.
  - `codecov_patch_only`: The only coverage gate that could reach 50 percent is a Codecov patch status. It bounds coverage of the changed lines only, and removing a test changes none, so it says nothing about the floor on total coverage. To have the coverage gate measured, run a coverage threshold of at least 50 percent in a CI step. Examples are pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80, or a fail_under your CI runs. Or add a numeric target to a Codecov project status.
  - `status_check_unconfirmed`: The coverage gate of at least 50 percent is a Codecov status target, and no CI line runs it. Codecov posts it as a commit status. It holds a merge only when branch protection requires it, and this scan does not read branch protection. Nothing to change if the Codecov status is a required check. To have the coverage gate measured, also run the threshold in a CI step (pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80).
  - `root_coverage_config_unresolved`: A scoped run found a fail_under in the root coverage.py config for a Python package with none of its own, not where CI runs coverage. coverage.py reads the config of the directory it runs in. So the root floor counts only when CI runs coverage from the root or names that config. Run coverage in CI from the repository root (pytest --cov, coverage report), or pass the root config with --cov-config or --rcfile; or give the package its own fail_under and run coverage from its directory or with --cov-config naming that config.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `coverage_gate.enforced_meets_minimum` feeds `layer-6-coverage.1:coverage_gate.enforced_meets_minimum`: An enforced floor turns the job red when a change takes coverage below it, so tests an agent removes or skips show in CI instead of passing quietly.

### `doc_staleness`: Doc staleness

It compares each doc's last change with the churn in the code it describes, so a doc whose code moved on is found before an agent relies on it.

- `doc_staleness.summary.stale_pct` feeds `doc-freshness.1:doc_staleness.summary.stale_pct`: An agent reads the docs as true. A doc whose code has moved on misleads it about that code.
- `doc_staleness.summary.stale_pct` feeds `doc-freshness.2:doc_staleness.summary.stale_pct`: With four in five mapped docs keeping pace with their code, an agent can take most of what it reads at its word.

### `repo_guards`: Ratchets and repo-owned guards

A ratchet or a boundary checker the repository runs in CI turns a structure rule into a red check, so an agent cannot quietly add one more suppression or cross one more layer. A guard with no test of its own can stop catching anything and still pass.

Each ratchet or repo-owned guard a CI job runs on ordinary changes. It follows the scripts, make recipes and local actions a step leads to. A guard is a lint baseline CI reads and a tracked command updates, a boundary checker, or a file-size cap. A boundary checker is import-boss, lint-imports, a check-layers script or an architecture test CI runs. It also reads whether each guard script has a test file of its own.

- Collector: `core.repo_guards`, reading `repo_root`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `repo_guards.guard_tested_reason` token, `repo_guards.guards.kind` token, `repo_guards.guards.path` path, `repo_guards.guards.script` path, `repo_guards.guards.target` path, `repo_guards.guards.tested_by` path, `repo_guards.guards.trigger` token, `repo_guards.guards.via` token, `repo_guards.present_reason` token.

- Evidence: `repo_guards.guard_tested` head_structure (measured), `repo_guards.present` head_structure (measured).
- Not measured when:
  - `ci_not_read`: No guard was found, and something here may run one that this reader cannot see. That is a CI file of a system it does not parse, or a .gitlab-ci.yml include: it does not follow. It can also be a step it could not settle, such as a remote reusable workflow. Nothing to change: this reads as not measured until that configuration can be read.
  - `trigger_unknown`: A guard was found only in a workflow or GitLab job whose trigger this reader could not settle. So it cannot say the guard runs on ordinary changes. Nothing to change: give the workflow a literal on: list of push or pull_request, or the GitLab job literal rules, for it to be read.
  - `no_guard_script`: Every guard found is a third-party tool or an architecture test with no committed script of its own. So there is no guard script whose tests to look for. Nothing to change: a third-party tool is tested where it is built.
  - `scan_failed`: The reader of ratchets and repo-owned guards raised an error, so both conditions read not measured. Nothing to change in the repository: report the error so the reader can be fixed.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `repo_guards.guard_tested` feeds `repo-guard-tested.1:repo_guards.guard_tested`: A guard script with no tests can stop catching anything and still pass, so a green check means less than it says. With its own tests, a change that breaks the guard turns red.

- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `structure.breakup_candidates.clusters` path, `structure.breakup_candidates.package` path, `structure.footprints.module` path, `structure.internal_burrow_edges.imported` path, `structure.internal_burrow_edges.importer` path, `structure.language` token, `structure.modularity_reason` token, `structure.name_collisions.name` path, `structure.name_collisions.paths` path, `structure.package_edges.from` path, `structure.package_edges.to` path, `structure.packages.id` path, `structure.reason` reason, `structure.sccs` path.

- Not measured when:
  - `no_grimp`: grimp, the Python import-graph builder, is not installed. Install the assess skill's Python dependencies (uv run does this) and run again.
  - `no_networkx`: networkx, which the structure metrics need, is not installed. Install the assess skill's Python dependencies (uv run does this) and run again.
  - `grimp_failed`: grimp could not build the Python import graph. Check that the packages import cleanly; the sentence after the code names grimp's error.
  - `no_python_packages`: A Python repository with no importable package. Nothing to change if the code is scripts; a package with an __init__.py is measured.
  - `no_builder:<language>`: No import graph builder covers the dominant source language, for example no_builder:java; no other language's graph stands in, and the sentence names a tool that would build one where one is known, jdeps for the JVM languages. Nothing to change: structure reads as not measured for this language.
  - `no_import_graph_<language>`: A builder covers the dominant source language but found nothing to graph in it, for example no_import_graph_go. Nothing to change if that code is loose scripts; a package the builder recognises is measured.
  - `invalid_import_graph`: A builder returned a graph that breaks the module-graph contract. Report it against the toolkit; structure reads as not measured meanwhile.
  - `no_source_files`: The scope holds no source file in a language the assess skill recognises. Nothing to change if the scope has no code; check the scope and the excludes otherwise.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `structure.modularity_q` feeds `layer-2-design.1:structure.modularity_q`: Clear modules let an agent load the part of the code a task touches, instead of tracing the whole repository to change one thing.
- `structure.cross_package_edges` feeds `layer-2-design.2:structure.cross_package_edges`: A guard for the next condition: with no import between packages, the front-door share reads null by default and says nothing about how packages are entered.
- `structure.front_door_ratio` feeds `layer-2-design.2:structure.front_door_ratio`: When packages are entered through one public surface, an agent can change a package's insides without breaking callers it never read.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `structure_drift.tier_0.boundary_patterns` feeds `layer-4-architecture.1:structure_drift.tier_0.boundary_patterns`: A map that names module paths tells an agent which code belongs together, and with CODEOWNERS, whose review a change there needs.

### `test_focus`: Test focus

It ranks risky files by the test work each needs, so the files where an agent's change is least held by tests come first.

- Collector: `core.test_focus`, reading `repo_root`, `current`, `coverage_data`, `test_pressure`, `hot_test_index`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: only a full /assess run builds it; headless and fleet runs report it not measured.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `test_focus.entries.hollow_heuristic_kinds` token, `test_focus.entries.risk_band` token, `test_focus.entries.suggested_action` token, `test_focus.entries.test_signal` token.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when:
  - `not_registered`: Only a full /assess run builds this block; a headless or fleet run reports it not measured. Run /assess on the repository to measure it.

### `test_pressure`: Test pressure

Coverage says a line ran, not that a test would notice it changing; this reads mutation results and hollow-test patterns to show where tests hold the code to account.

- Collector: `core.test_pressure`, reading `test_pressure_scan`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: only a full /assess run builds it; headless and fleet runs report it not measured.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.assertion_on_internal.confidence` token, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.assertion_on_internal.internal_field` drop, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.assertion_on_internal.subject_function` drop, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.confidence_note` drop, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.duplicate_truth.confidence` token, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.duplicate_truth.derives_from` drop, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.duplicate_truth.field_name` drop, `test_pressure.cheap_heuristics.untested_boundaries.operator` token, `test_pressure.gap_signal` token, `test_pressure.mutation_groups.config` token, `test_pressure.mutation_groups.reason` drop, `test_pressure.mutation_groups.root` path, `test_pressure.mutation_groups.runner` token, `test_pressure.mutation_groups.scope` path, `test_pressure.mutation_groups.unmeasured` path, `test_pressure.mutation_note` drop, `test_pressure.mutation_scope` path, `test_pressure.mutation_tools_detected` token, `test_pressure.reason` drop.
- Used by: row `layer-6-coverage`, finding `untrusted_hotspot`.
- Evidence: `test_pressure.mutation_run` execution_artifact (measured).
- Not measured when:
  - `not_registered`: Only a full /assess run builds this block; a headless or fleet run reports it not measured. Run /assess on the repository to measure it.

Why the signals named here matter:

- `test_pressure.mutation_run` feeds `layer-6-coverage.2:test_pressure.mutation_run`: Coverage shows tests run the code; a mutation run shows whether they notice it changing. A completed run names the surviving mutants, which are the tests an agent cannot yet rely on.

### `understanding`: Keyhole blocks: understanding

For each complex module it reads whether a person authored it and whether a doc states its intent, so an agent knows whether there is anyone or anything to check its reading against.

- Collector: `core.keyhole_blocks`, reading `keyhole`, `run_scope`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: only a full /assess run builds it; headless and fleet runs report it not measured.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `understanding.authorship_class_by_path.{}` token, `understanding.modules.authorship_class` token, `understanding.modules.finding` token, `understanding.modules.recommendation` drop, `understanding.orphaned_understanding` path, `understanding.reason` drop.
- Used by: finding `orphaned_understanding`.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when:
  - `not_registered`: Only a full /assess run builds this block; a headless or fleet run reports it not measured. Run /assess on the repository to measure it.

### `unit_readings`: Monorepo unit readings

A unit inherits root CI and review but not the root's suppressions, stale docs or structure. Reading those per unit, with each condition labelled, shows which change lifts which unit.

Each unit's own readings of the scope-sensitive scans: suppressions, doc staleness, structure, size, and its own coverage gate or instruction file. Every condition is tagged unit or inherited.

- Collector: `core.unit_readings`, reading `units`, `nested_instructions`, `coverage_gate`, `doc_staleness`, `layer_grades`, `promissory_markers`, `skill_disclosure`, `skill_personal_data`, `skill_script_tests`, `stats_summary`, `structure`, `excludes`, `repo_root`, `working_notes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: only with assess_signals --units (or --scans naming it) or fleet --monorepo-units; left out otherwise.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `unit_readings.unit_blocks` token, `unit_readings.unit_count_reason` token, `unit_readings.units.conditions.id` token, `unit_readings.units.conditions.origin` token, `unit_readings.units.kind` token, `unit_readings.units.path` hashed_path.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

### `units`: Monorepo units

One score for a monorepo describes none of its services. Naming each unit lets every one be scored on its own, so one service's gaps are not hidden behind another's practices.

The repository's units. First each skill folder (a SKILL.md), and a plugin's agents/ and commands/. Then the shallowest build-manifest folders, with each workspace root's declared members in its place, or the [[units]] of .assess/config.toml. Folders with only a manifest are skipped.

- Collector: `core.units`, reading `repo_root`, `excludes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: only with assess_signals --units (or --scans naming it) or fleet --monorepo-units; left out otherwise.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `units.aggregators.ecosystem` token, `units.aggregators.path` drop, `units.skipped.path` drop, `units.skipped.problem` token, `units.source` token, `units.unit_count_reason` token, `units.units.ecosystem` token, `units.units.kind` token, `units.units.name` drop, `units.units.origin` token, `units.units.path` hashed_path, `units.units.workspace` drop, `units.unreadable_manifests` drop.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

## Derived findings

Sorted by name.

| Finding | Reads | Why it matters | Next step | Mode | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accretion_ratchet` Accretion ratchet | `accretion_ratchet` | A file that has only ever grown gets harder to read whole with each change, and each agent addition makes the next one harder. | make the file smaller: move code out, delete dead code, or split the file | `refactor_safe` | - |
| `candidate_dead_weight` Candidate dead weight | `dead_code` | Code nothing in the repository calls costs an agent reading time and can be maintained by mistake; it needs a person to confirm no outside caller uses it. | check that the code is used, and delete it if it is not | `verify_then_retire` | - |
| `hidden_coupling` Hidden coupling | `behaviour.hidden_coupling_findings`, `structure_drift.tier_1` | These files change together in history with no import between them, so an agent changing one has nothing in the code telling it to change the other. | check why these files change together | `characterize_first` | emptied when `doc_staleness.churn_degenerate == true`; deleted paths pruned; thresholds `high_front_door_ratio` 0.7, `high_modularity_q` 0.3, `low_containment` 0.3 |
| `lying_map` Stale doc over complex code | `documentation.stale_doc_on_complexity` | The doc has fallen behind complex code it describes, which is where an agent leans on a doc most. | fix or delete the doc | `verify_then_retire` | emptied when `doc_staleness.churn_degenerate == true` |
| `orphaned_understanding` Orphaned understanding | `understanding.orphaned_understanding` | Complex code with no human author and no doc of its intent has nobody to ask and nothing to check an agent's reading against. | name a person who owns this code before it changes again | `characterize_first` | - |
| `override_contradicts_signals` Archetype override contradicts the signals | `archetype` | The declared repository kind decides which checks apply; when the signals disagree, checks marked not applicable may hide gaps an agent would meet. | Review the archetype marker: the measured signals suggest a different kind of repository | `characterize_first` | - |
| `refactor_boundary` Refactor boundary | `behaviour.refactor_boundaries` | A strength: edits here stay inside the directory, so an agent can change it without reading the rest of the repository. | safe to hand an agent in isolation | `refactor_safe` | deleted paths pruned; a strength, not a concern |
| `self_referential_tests` Self-referential tests | `current` | Tests kept and committed beside the code they cover can check internal consistency rather than truth, so an agent changing both together can make them agree on a wrong answer. | ask a person to review: the tests check that the code agrees with itself, not that it is right | `verify_then_retire` | - |
| `unactioned_intent` Unactioned intent | `promissory` | A TODO or skip that survives many edits reads to an agent as a live plan or a settled exception, and it cannot tell which. | keep the promise: fix it, open a ticket for it, or delete the marker or skip | `verify_then_retire` | - |
| `unexplained_complexity` Unexplained complexity | `documentation.unexplained_complexity` | Complex code with no doc of what it should do leaves an agent only the code to infer intent from, so it cannot tell a bug from a requirement. | write the contract the code needs (write it by hand; do not generate it) | `characterize_first` | - |
| `untrusted_hotspot` Untrusted hotspot | `current`, `test_pressure` | Complex, often-changed code whose tests let many mutants survive: an agent's change here is not held by the tests that look like they cover it. | make the tests check what the code does, as a caller sees it (not its internal state) | `characterize_first` | - |
